effort: Produce a short forward push and receive it under a controlled stance position without an external drop or run-up.
brief: After the prescribed linked-contact emphasis, this class restores isolated receiving. E1 anchors the coordinated countermovement forward push. Raised receiving, nominated single-leg receiving, low obstacle clearance, a stationary split-stance exchange and a grounded preload-to-rebound task expose different foot-placement demands. Primary step-up strength supports raising body mass through the stance leg; the remainder retains ankle, hinge and leg-recovery roles.
marker: Count controlled finishes within each two-attempt set: one dip and coordinated arms, two-foot landing beneath the body held for 2 s without an extra step. Keep the modest chosen distance repeatable; farther is not automatically better for this support task.
review: Class 7 prescribed 29 landings, twelve single-leg receiving events and linked alternatives, but no actual completion is known. Class 8 restores full resets and uses only four single-leg receiving events. The new main step-up uses the same 2 × 6 per-leg working count as the earlier split-squat anchor; the task change is conditional, not an automatic load progression.
sequence: E1 is first with two sets; the more demanding nominated-leg receiving follows a shared raised landing task while fresh. The final three tasks have small doses and full resets; no long horizontal or switching-lunge circuit.

E.name: Broad Jump to Stick — countermovement with arms
E.job: Main integrated forward push with coordinated hip/knee extension and arm action, followed by owned receiving.
E.cue: One smooth dip, swing arms forward and jump a modest distance; bring both feet under the body and hold 2 s. No reaching heels far ahead. Shorten distance for a backward fall or extra step; no maximum-distance test.

E.name: Single-Leg Forward Jump to Low Box — two-foot landing
E.family: unilateral push with raised shared receiving
E.job: Express each leg's forward/upward push while using a low raised two-foot finish to reduce fall distance.
E.cue: Start close to a very low stable box, one-foot push, land with both feet flat on top without tucking and hold 2 s. Step down. Lower target/shorten gap for knee tuck or a cramped landing; do not jump off the box.

E.name: Two-Foot Forward Jump to Single-Leg Stick
E.job: Concentrate a small forward receiving demand on one stance leg while sharing the takeoff effort.
E.cue: Very low two-foot forward push, no more than one own foot length; land on the nominated foot underneath the pelvis and hold 2 s. Reduce travel/flight for collapse or extra steps. This needs demonstrated current single-leg receiving control.

E.name: Single Low Hurdle Jump to Stick
E.job: Clear a small obstacle through a purposeful push and place both feet accurately without a rebound demand.
E.cue: One suitably low hurdle, stationary two-foot takeoff, land just beyond and hold 2 s. No preceding bounce or linked second jump. Lower/remove the hurdle rather than tucking knees or stretching the landing.

E.name: Split Jump Switch to Stick
E.job: Change which leg receives the lead support role during a short, controlled explosive stance exchange.
E.cue: Small split stance, shallow dip, low jump and exchange lead legs once; land in a short split stance and hold 2 s. Reset before another jump. No traveling, repeated jumping-lunge rhythm or maximal depth; reduce stance length for twisting.

E.name: Grounded Snap-Down to Low Rebound Jump
E.job: Organize a rapid lowering into a responsive push without adding the energy of a drop from a box.
E.cue: Start tall with heels lightly raised but forefeet grounded; quickly settle heels and bend hips/knees slightly, then make one small vertical rebound jump and stick 2 s. The initial snap-down has no flight. Reduce speed/depth if alignment is lost; no extra pogo afterward.

S.name: Lateral Step-Down — low heel tap
S.job: Lightly strengthen knee/pelvis alignment during lowering into the stance leg.
S.cue: Use a low stable step, free heel reaches beside the box; lower 3 s and rise 1 s without pushing from the free heel. Reduce range for hip drop. Use supported shallow single-leg squat instead if no suitable low step exists, same dose and tempo.

S.name: Short-Lever Hamstring Bridge Hold
S.job: Light hamstring/pelvic support before the stronger hinge and walkout tasks.
S.cue: Supine with heels close and knees well bent; gently lift hips to a low comfortable bridge while pressing heels down. Hold level with easy breathing, not maximal effort. Lower height/bring heels closer for cramp or back arch; ten seconds is a hold, not ten reps.

P.name: Dumbbell Step-Up
P.cue: Use a stable low box placing the working thigh below horizontal; whole foot on top. Rise 1 s using the upper leg, lower 3 s; no push/jump from the trailing foot. Reduce load/height for pelvic hike. If no suitable low box exists, use floor Split Squat instead at the same working/preparation counts and tempo; record the different task.
P.job: Primary stance-leg force: raise body mass through a supported forward foot placement.
P.decision: Earlier split squat 2 × 6 per leg → low DB step-up 2 × 6 per leg. Working count is unchanged; establish step height and load from current control. The floor split-squat replacement preserves the count if the box is unsuitable.

P.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift — hand supported, dumbbell
P.cue: One DB opposite working leg, free hand on stable support. Soft stance knee, free leg travels back, pelvis faces floor; lower 3 s and rise 1 s. Support removes balance as the limiter. Reduce load/range for hip opening or trunk rotation.
P.job: Maintain a supported one-leg hip hinge so receiving stance is backed by loadable hip force.

P.name: Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated dumbbells
P.cue: Both legs together, knees near 90°, heels start on floor, hands secure DBs on lower thighs above knees. Rise 1 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s. Reduce load for bounce/lost heel height. If bench fit is unsuitable, use supported standing bent-knee calf raises instead, same reps/rest, and log changed knee angle.
P.job: Keep controlled knee-flexed ankle force after the isolated receiving work.

P.name: Standing Dumbbell Calf Raise — supported single leg
P.cue: Work from floor, near-straight soft knee, one DB and stable hand support. Rise 1 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s. Reduce load or use bodyweight for lost range; use 1 × 8 bilateral instead of per-leg work if even unilateral bodyweight is too demanding, with 1 × 4 bilateral preparation.
P.job: Retain a limited straight-knee calf force role without additional impacts.

P.name: Glute Bridge Walkout
P.cue: Keep a floor bridge while four small alternating heel steps go out and four return; eight steps at about 1 s each = one full cycle. Choose reach so four cycles are challenging with 2–3 whole cycles available. Shorten reach for pelvic sag or cramping; do not add steps or cycles.
P.job: Challenge knee-flexor control through changing lever length after the brief easy hold.

P.name: Supine Band-resisted Hip Flexion
P.cue: Secure loop band around both forefeet; nonworking leg straight with heel grounded. Flex working hip/knee toward thigh-vertical in 2 s, hold 1 s, return 2 s without arching or moving the anchor heel. Reduce tension/range for pelvic tilt. If a secure loop is unavailable, use seated DB hip flexion instead with hands securing the DB above the knee: same dose/rest, small controlled thigh lift; preparation unloaded.
P.job: Maintain resisted leg recovery with the pelvis stabilized.

equipment: All boxes/hurdles must fit the athlete and be stable; no minimum jump height is required. E2 without a suitable low box uses same-leg forward push to a two-foot floor landing instead, same 1 × 2 per takeoff leg/rest, four two-foot events. E3 uses a two-foot receiving landing instead when one-leg control is insufficient, 1 × 4 total with 20 s resets and 120 s afterward; four events remain but add four individual foot contacts. Remove E4's hurdle instead of adding height. Use a no-switch Split-Squat Jump to Stick instead of E5 if stance exchange is not controlled, same counts/rest. E6 uses a slower grounded lowering before the single jump instead if rapid preload fails; no extra flight.
count_note: Default landings: E1 four + E2 four + E3 four + E4 two + E5 four + E6 three = 21 events: 17 two-foot, four single-leg, 38 individual foot contacts. E2 adds four grounded box descents. E6 has three nonflight snap-downs plus three airborne-jump landings; heel settling is not an extra jump. E5 always lands on two feet despite switching lead leg. These receiving types are not equal mechanical loads.
novelty: The default drills add integrated countermovement forward push, raised shared receiving after one-leg propulsion, two-to-one forward receiving, isolated hurdle clearance, a single split-stance exchange and grounded preload-to-rebound. They are meaningful variants of earlier jump families with changed force-sharing, clearance or coupling, not arbitrary new labels. Returning simpler floor/no-switch mechanics as readiness replacements is intentional.
audit: Reduced unilateral receiving to four events after Class 7's linked emphasis and rejected any external box drop. A possible repeated split-switch sequence was reduced to isolated single switches with full rest. The grounded snap-down is separated from its one actual landing in the workload count. New main step-up is conditional on box fit and leg-dominant execution; no load or depth is presumed earned.
progression: Use current technical control to select each receiving route. Keep a consistent step height/stance and record the load if performed; no future percentage increase is scheduled. Class 9 can emphasize rapid force against light external resistance while reducing landing exposure, provided the implement can be handled securely.
map_note: Isolated forward receiving; four single-leg landings and a conditional main step-up.
next_job: Rapid force against manageable external resistance with low landing exposure.
handoff: Review Class 8's receiving variants, step-up setup and any actual response, then finalize and save Class 9 before proceeding.

final_review: Reviewed isolated receiving after the linked class. The default has 21 landings with only four single-leg receiving events; snap-downs start grounded and do not add hidden jumps. Split switches are individual reset attempts, not a running or lunge circuit. Main step-up and all raised targets have defined floor replacements. No external depth drop, automatic height increase or earned-load claim is present.
